questions.enonce_markdown:
**(i)** The probability distribution of a discrete random variable $X$ is given by

$$P(X = x) = \begin{cases} k(x+1), & x = 1, 2, 3, \\ k(x-3), & x = 4, 5, 6, \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$

Find (a) the value of the constant $k$.

**(ii)** Of the large number of candidates applying for a job in an enterprise, 5% are qualified. The candidates are interviewed one after another until the first qualified applicant is interviewed.

(d) Find the mean number of applicants interviewed.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Because the number of candidates is large, each interviewed candidate is qualified independently with probability $p = 0.05$. Let $N$ be the number of candidates interviewed up to and including the first qualified one: $N$ has a **geometric distribution** with parameter $p = 0.05$,

$$P(N = n) = (1 - p)^{n-1}p = (0.95)^{n-1}(0.05), \qquad n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$$

Its mean is $E(N) = \dfrac{1}{p}$ (from $\sum_{n \ge 1} n q^{n-1}p = \dfrac{p}{(1 - q)^2} = \dfrac{1}{p}$ with $q = 1 - p$).

$$E(N) = \frac{1}{0.05} = 20$$

**The mean number of applicants interviewed is $20$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) Calculate, to four decimal places, the probability that the fifth candidate interviewed is the first qualified applicant.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first qualified applicant is the fifth one interviewed when the first four are not qualified and the fifth is qualified:

$$P(N = 5) = (0.95)^4(0.05) = 0.81450625 \times 0.05 = 0.0407253\ldots$$

**$P(N = 5) = 0.0407$ (4 d.p.).**
